definitions.explanation: Damage caused to oneself or one's own property, without involvement of another party. Most commonly used in traffic and insurance contexts.

examples.japanese: {自損|じそん}⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{起|お}こした→起こす：01234_okosu⟧。
{自損|じそん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{場合|ばあい}→場合：01704_baai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{保険|ほけん}→保険：01509_hoken⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{適用|てきよう}されない→適用する：21739_tekiyousuru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: In cases of self-inflicted damage, insurance may not apply.

examples.japanese: ⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧スリップ⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{電柱|でんちゅう}→電柱：17913_denchuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ぶつかる→ぶつかる：02412_butsukaru⟧{自損|じそん}⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多発|たはつ}→多発：20508_tahatsu⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: There has been a rash of single-vehicle accidents where cars slip on rain and hit utility poles.

notes:
A compound of {自|じ} (self) and ⟦{損|そん}→損：03325_son⟧ (damage, loss). Primarily used in traffic and insurance contexts to describe accidents or damage involving only the person responsible, with no other parties affected.

The most common usage is {自損|じそん}⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧ (single-vehicle accident), referring to crashes where the driver hits a guardrail, pole, wall, or ditch without colliding with another vehicle or person.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自損|じそん}⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧: single-vehicle accident; self-caused accident
- {自損|じそん}⟦{行為|こうい}→行為：10021_koui⟧: self-inflicted act
- {自損|じそん}⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦{届|とど}け→届ける：01248_todokeru⟧: single-vehicle accident report

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{物損|ぶっそん}→物損：24642_busson⟧: property damage — damage to things (as opposed to personal injury)
- ⟦{人身|じんしん}{事故|じこ}→人身事故：08475_jinshinjiko⟧: personal injury accident — an accident involving bodily harm
- ⟦{追突|ついとつ}→追突：17054_tsuitotsu⟧: rear-end collision — a specific type of traffic accident involving another vehicle
